expectations.text: The response identifies that python datetime values are bound as TIMESTAMP and compared to a DATE column, so Oracle applies INTERNAL_FUNCTION to the column and cannot use IDX_ORDERS_DATE
expectations.evidence: 'The driver sends your Python datetime values as TIMESTAMP, and the column is DATE. Oracle then has to convert the column (INTERNAL_FUNCTION("ORDER_DATE")) ... an index on order_date can't seek on a converted column.'

expectations.text: The response fixes it by binding as DATE (e.g. cursor.setinputsizes(start_ts=oracledb.DB_TYPE_DATE, ...)) or by CAST(:start_ts AS DATE) / TO_DATE on the parameter side
expectations.evidence: Option A cur.setinputsizes(start_ts=oracledb.DB_TYPE_DATE, end_ts=oracledb.DB_TYPE_DATE); Option B CAST(:start_ts AS DATE).

expectations.text: The response says rebuilding the index will not help
expectations.evidence: 'Not a broken or bloated index... A rebuild only costs you an outage window.'

expectations.text: The response says a hint is not the right fix (or not needed once the bind type is fixed)
expectations.evidence: 'Not something a hint can fix. /*+ INDEX(...) */ can't turn INTERNAL_FUNCTION(col) >= :b into a range seek.'

expectations.text: The response explains why the SQL Developer test with literal dates uses the index (the literals are DATE, so no conversion)
expectations.evidence: 'Literals in SQL Developer use the index because DATE '2026-11-23' or TO_DATE(...) is a DATE. The types match, nothing is converted'.

expectations.text: The response gives verification with DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY_CURSOR and says what to expect: INDEX RANGE SCAN with access(...) predicates and peeked binds of type DATE
expectations.evidence: DISPLAY_CURSOR(..., 'ALLSTATS LAST +PEEKED_BINDS'); expects 'Peeked Binds show (DATE)', 'INDEX RANGE SCAN | IDX_ORDERS_DATE with access("ORDER_DATE">=:START_TS ...) and no INTERNAL_FUNCTION'.

expectations.text: The response does not recommend creating a new index as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: Covering index is 'Optional ... only if this query is hot' and 'Don't do this until fix 1 is in'; primary fix is bind type.

expectations.text: Each reported issue carries an explicit severity label (e.g. High / Medium / Low, or Critical / Major / Minor); ordering alone does not count
expectations.evidence: Issues table Severity column: 'High' for bind mismatch, 'Low (optional)' for non-covering.

overall_notes: none. Correctly notes ALLSTATS LAST needs GATHER_PLAN_STATISTICS/STATISTICS_LEVEL=ALL and that the DATE bind creates a new child cursor.
